chunks: A number of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Sabbah al-Muzani, from al-Harith ibn Haseerah, from al-Asbagh, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he wanted to rebuke a man, would say: 'By Allah, you are even more deficient than the one who neglects the ghusl on Friday, and indeed he remains in purity until the next Friday.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of neglecting the Friday ritual bath (Ghusl) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs a rhetorical comparison to emphasize the spiritual gravity of neglecting the Friday ritual bath (Ghusl al-Jumu'ah). He asserts that the one who omits it is more deficient than the one who performs it, as the latter maintains a continuous state of ritual purity throughout the week until the next Friday. This highlights the Friday Ghusl not merely as a preparatory act, but as a sustaining spiritual state in Shia jurisprudence.
